items.title: Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers

The agency's operators gained access to the criminal's operation's backend and cut it off from those computers. "The next steps that we took were to disconnect that Amadey controller from all those
items.summary: Australian authorities disrupted the backend operation of the Amadey malware, cutting off access to 180,000 infected computers worldwide. Monitor threat intelligence feeds for indicators of compromise related to Amadey.

items.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
items.snippet: OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown. OpenAI's reasoning models work through a problem before answering, and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read. The method got past
items.summary: A security flaw in OpenAI's compaction feature allowed researchers to bypass hidden reasoning protections and extract raw reasoning data. Review LLM integration handling and monitor OpenAI for security advisories.

items.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
items.snippet: Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account. Microsoft tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-80097 and fixed it in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246, so anyone using the app should update. In the researchers' tests,
items.summary: A vulnerability in Microsoft Authenticator for Android allowed permissionless apps to steal work account sign-in tokens. Upgrade Authenticator for Android to the fixed version or later.

items.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
items.snippet: Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations. Some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords. They can also capture MFA codes or hijack authenticated sessions, allowing attackers to gain
items.summary: Generative AI is being leveraged by attackers to create more convincing and tailored fake login pages for phishing and account takeovers. Review and strengthen anti-phishing controls and multi-factor authentication requirements.

items.title: dcmjs: DS/IS VALUE REPRESENTATION INPUT VALIDATION BYPASS
items.snippet: dcmjs, a JavaScript library for DICOM manipulation used in web-based medical imaging viewers, contains an input validation bypass in its handling of DS (Decimal String) and IS (Integer String) value representations. The DecimalString and IntegerString classes in ValueRepresentation.js use a regex sanitizer followed by JavaScript's Number() constructor. While the regex strips direct NaN/Infinity s…
items.summary: An input validation bypass in dcmjs affects web-based medical imaging viewers handling DICOM files. Upgrade dcmjs to 0.52.0 or later.

items.title: OAuthLib: Bearer token can be retrieved as long as client knows a valid client ID for device workflow
items.snippet: A call to the token endpoint with a grant type of `"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code"` and a bogus `device_code` is able to get a bearer token as long as they know a valid client ID enabled for the device workflow. [Section 3.4 of the RFC 8628 spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628#section-3.4) says that the token endpoint should take in `device_code` as a required parame…
items.summary: An OAuthLib vulnerability allows retrieving a bearer token using a bogus device code if a valid client ID is known. Upgrade oauthlib to 4.0.0 or later.

items.title: MONAILabel Server Crash and Silent Inference Corruption via Crafted DICOM (pydicom DS/IS Validation Bypass)
items.snippet: An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash a running MONAILabel server or silently corrupt its medical AI inference results by uploading a single crafted DICOM file (~132 KB) via the REST API. The vulnerability stems from pydicom's lack of validation for Decimal String (DS) and Integer String (IS) DICOM Value Representations, which allows NaN and infinity values to pass through MONAI's PydicomR…
items.summary: A lack of validation in pydicom affects MONAILabel servers, enabling remote attackers to crash the server or corrupt AI inference results. Upgrade monai to 1.6.1 or later.

items.title: Agno: Arbitrary code execution via `eval()` on `field_type` in `FunctionCall`

This is a code injection flaw (CWE-95) with full impact to confidentiality, in…
items.summary: Agno versions prior to 2.3.24 contain an arbitrary code execution vulnerability via Python's built-in eval() function in the model execution component, affecting developers using Agno. Upgrade agno to 2.3.24 or later.

items.title: Nodemailer: Quadratic backtracking in SMTP AUTH mechanism detection regexes allows pre-auth remote denial of service
items.snippet: Nodemailer's SMTP client applies four regular expressions to a peer's EHLO response to detect the supported SASL mechanisms. Each pattern uses an alternation with two overlapping whitespace-matching sub-patterns, which produces quadratic (O(n^2)) backtracking whenever the mechanism name is absent from the line. A malicious or MITM SMTP server that answers EHLO with `250-AUTH` followed by a long w…
items.summary: Nodemailer has a quadratic backtracking vulnerability in SMTP AUTH mechanism detection regexes affecting Node.js developers. Upgrade nodemailer to 10.0.13 or later.

items.title: Nodemailer: RFC 5322 comment inside an angle-bracket address is never stripped
items.snippet: Nodemailer's address parser has three published, patched fixes for RFC 5322 comment `(...)` handling inside an addr-spec: GHSA-cc9r-2j5m-2m83 (comment glued two domain atoms into one), GHSA-g57g-f23g-4646 (the same glue for a quoted local part), and the related ReDoS fixes GHSA-prgh-xp8r-p3m5 / GHSA-v53p-9fqp-m79j. All three fixes live in `_handleAddress()`'s `joins` / `_recoverAddrSpec()` logic…
items.summary: Nodemailer fails to strip RFC 5322 comments inside angle-bracket addresses, impacting Node.js applications. Upgrade nodemailer to 10.0.13 or later.

items.title: Nodemailer: Quadratic (O(n^2)) SMTP client reply parsing lets a malicious server or MITM cause a pre-auth remote denial of service
items.snippet: The SMTP client response parser reassembles multiline server replies by appending each continuation line onto a single response-queue entry and re-testing whether that entry is still a partial (continuation) reply on every line. The partial-response test runs `str.slice(str.lastIndexOf('\n') + 1)` on the growing entry, which forces a full flatten of the entire accumulated string on each line. A m…
items.summary: Nodemailer contains a quadratic SMTP client reply parsing issue that can cause a pre-auth denial of service. Upgrade nodemailer to 10.0.10 or later.

items.title: better-auth: Device login approval does not show the requesting client or permissions
items.snippet: You may be affected if you use `better-auth` from `1.3.8-beta.3` up to, but not including, `1.7.0-rc.3`, and you enable the `deviceAuthorization()` plugin. items.title: Satori-generated SVG has improper escaping
items.snippet: Satori does not properly escape certain values before including them in generated SVG output. This can allow crafted values to be interpreted as SVG markup. The impact depends on how the generated SVG is consumed. No complete workaround exists besides upgrading. Applications that cannot immediately upgrade should not render attacker-controlled content with Satori.
items.summary: Satori generates SVGs with improper escaping which can allow crafted values to be interpreted as markup. Upgrade satori to 0.33.5 or later.

items.title: Ghost: Authorization Bypass in Comment Like Feature
items.snippet: An input validation issue allowed members to delete comment likes / dislikes that they were not authorized to delete. This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.9.0 up to v6.44.1. v6.44.1 contains a fix for this issue. For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://do…
items.summary: Ghost has an authorization bypass allowing members to delete comment likes/dislikes without proper permissions. Upgrade ghost to 6.44.1 or later.

items.title: GitPython: Submodule.move() follows an attacker-committed intermediate symlink outside the worktree
items.snippet: GitPython's public `Submodule.move()` API verifies that its destination is lexically inside the parent repository, but it does not reject symbolic links in the destination's intermediate components before filesystem operations. On systems that check out Git symlinks, an untrusted repository can therefore redirect a fixed, application-selected move destination outside the parent worktree. The repo…
items.summary: GitPython's Submodule.move() follows attacker-committed intermediate symlinks outside the worktree. Upgrade GitPython to 3.2.0 or later.

items.title: GitPython Remote.pull() refspec bypasses the --upload-pack unsafe-option guard, enabling arbitrary command execution
items.snippet: `Remote.pull()` in GitPython forwards its positional `refspec` argument directly to the `git pull` child process while its unsafe-option guard inspects only keyword arguments. An application that passes attacker-influenced data as the `refspec` (for example a user-supplied branch or refspec parameter in a web or CI service) can supply an option-shaped value such as `--upload-pack= `. The value by…
items.summary: GitPython Remote.pull() refspec bypasses unsafe-option guards, enabling arbitrary command execution. Upgrade GitPython to 3.2.0 or later.

items.title: GitPython command wrappers omit unsafe protocol and option checks
items.snippet: GitPython has spent 2022-2026 rolling out two reusable guards method-by-method: `Git.check_unsafe_protocols(url)` (raises `UnsafeProtocolError` for `::` remote-helper URLs - CVE-2022-24439) and `Git.check_unsafe_options(...)` (raises `UnsafeOptionError` for denylisted option spellings - CVE-2023-40267, CVE-2026-42215, CVE-2026-67323). Three wrapper methods that build a `git` argv from caller-cont…
items.summary: GitPython command wrappers omit unsafe protocol and option checks in certain scenarios. Upgrade GitPython to 3.2.0 or later.

items.title: GitPython: separate_git_dir leaks env vars via crafted .gitmodules submodule name
items.snippet: `Repo._clone()`'s handling of `separate_git_dir` never disables `Git.polish_url()`'s environment-variable expansion, unlike every other caller of that helper that handles attacker-influenced data. Since `separate_git_dir` can be derived from an attacker-controlled `.gitmodules` submodule name, a completely ordinary `clone` + `submodule_update(init=True, recursive=True)` on a malicious repository…
items.summary: GitPython separate_git_dir leaks environment variables via crafted .gitmodules submodule names. Upgrade GitPython to 3.2.0 or later.

items.title: GitPython parse_actor_and_date() is vulnerable to quadratic backtracking on malformed identity lines

items.summary: GitPython's parse_actor_and_date() is vulnerable to quadratic backtracking on malformed identity lines. Upgrade GitPython to 3.2.0 or later.

items.title: LiteLLM: Privilege Escalation to Proxy Admin via Cross-Domain Reuse of the Salt Key

The proxy uses one encryption key for two purposes: sealing secrets at rest and minting session tokens. An attacker exploits this by requesting a new API key with a crafted metadata field containing a forged admin credential as the "secret" value. The proxy encrypts and returns t…
items.summary: LiteLLM suffers from a privilege escalation vulnerability to Proxy Admin via cross-domain reuse of the salt key. Upgrade litellm to 1.100.4, 1.101.3, 1.102.2, 1.103.1, 1.104.0rc2 or later.

items.title: MessagePack: Unbounded memory leak in msgpack C extension on strict_map_key validation failure
items.snippet: The msgpack-python C extension (`msgpack._cmsgpack`) leaks a decoded map value when deserialization rejects a key with `strict_map_key=True` (the default). Both `unpackb()` and the streaming `Unpacker` API are affected. The pure-Python fa…
items.summary: MessagePack C extension leaks memory when strict_map_key validation fails during deserialization. Upgrade msgpack to 1.2.3 or later.

items.summary: NLTK WekaClassifier passes unvalidated paths to the Weka Java VM, bypassing containment checks. Upgrade nltk to 3.10.4 or later.

items.title: Authlib: empty signatures validation in JWS JSON deserialization

items.summary: Authlib accepts empty signatures in JWS JSON deserialization without cryptographic verification. Upgrade authlib to 1.9.0 or later.

items.title: Pylint: Arbitrary code execution via pickle deserialization of the stats cache in PYLINT_HOME
items.snippet: Since 2006 / pylint 0.15.2, pylint caches its stats as pickles in `PYLINT_HOME` and reload them on the next run with `pickle.load`. Someone without access to the configuration or linted code, but with access to the cache directory (predictable `PYLINT_HOME` on a multi-user host) can write a crafted pickle that will runs arbitrary code when pylint access its stat cache. From pylint 4.0.9, the resu…
items.summary: Pylint is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via pickle deserialization of the stats cache in PYLINT_HOME. Upgrade pylint to 4.0.9 or later.

items.title: vllm p2p never connected zmq_exhaustion

items.title: Rembg: Unauthenticated SAM model injection permits local-file disclosure through malicious ONNX graphs

items.title: fpdf2: Exponential SVG '<use>' expansion causes CPU and memory exhaustion in 'FPDF.image()'

items.summary: fpdf2 implicitly loads external URLs and local image paths when rendering untrusted content. Upgrade fpdf2 to 2.8.8 or later.

items.title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via failed HTTP/2 handshake

items.summary: The experimental WebSocket client in Node.js undici can cause a denial of service via a failed HTTP/2 handshake. Upgrade undici to 8.11.2 or later.

items.title: Authlib accepts an empty HMAC key, allowing JWS/JWT signature forgery (HS256/HS384/HS512)
items.snippet: Reporter: Cavan Loughran, Celvex Group Inc. Summary Authlib's symmetric (oct) key handling accepts an empty key (empty bytes b'' / empty string '') as a valid HMAC signing and verification key. An empty HMAC key produces a deterministic digest that any party can reproduce, so an attacker who knows (or can cause) the application to verify a token with an empty key can forge arbitrary tokens that p…
items.summary: Authlib permits an empty HMAC signing key, which allows remote attackers to forge JWS and JWT signatures. Upgrade Authlib to 1.9.1 or later.

items.title: Authlib: Unvalidated request_uri fetch in JWT-secured authorization request (JAR) leading to SSRF
items.snippet: Authlib's RFC 9101 (JAR) extension passes the attacker-controlled `request_uri` authorization parameter straight to the `get_request_object()` fetch hook with no validation, at a pre-authentication endpoint. Authlib already defines the pre-registration allowlist for this (`request_uris` client metadata and `require_request_uri_registration` server metadata) but the extension never consults it, an…
items.summary: Unvalidated request URI fetching in Authlib's JAR implementation enables server-side request forgery (SSRF). Upgrade authlib to 1.9.0 or later.

items.title: Authlib: ID token can disable its own nonce validation via the nonce_supported claim
items.snippet: `OpenIDMixin.parse_id_token()` reads the `nonce_supported` claim from the ID token it is validating. When that claim is boolean `false`, the expected nonce is set to `None` and nonce validation is skipped for that token. An ID token that carries this claim is therefore accepted in a session whose nonce does not match. A captured, validly signed ID token belonging to a victim can be replayed into…
items.summary: OpenID tokens in Authlib can disable their own nonce validation via a specific claim, leading to replay attacks. Upgrade authlib to 1.9.0 or later.

items.title: Authlib: Default JWT bearer grant accepts assertions for the wrong audience
items.snippet: Authlib's default RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant leaves `get_audiences()` empty, so `verify_claims()` only checks that an `aud` claim *exists* instead of requiring it to match the current authorization server's token endpoint. An attacker holding a legitimately issued JWT assertion for *any* audience can present it to a different authorization server sharing the same signing key and obtain an access t…
items.summary: Authlib's default JWT bearer grant accepts tokens intended for alternate audiences, breaking proper access boundaries. Upgrade authlib to 1.9.0 or later.

items.summary: An incomplete algorithm-confusion fix in Authlib permits HMAC forgery using prefixed asymmetric public keys. Upgrade authlib to 1.9.0 or later.

items.title: Authlib: is_secure_transport() loopback exemption can be bypassed with a userinfo component, allowing cleartext-HTTP URLs to non-loopback hosts
items.snippet: `authlib.common.security.is_secure_transport()` is used throughout Authlib to enforce the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC requirement that endpoint and redirect URIs use TLS, with an RFC 8252 §7.3 exemption for loopback `http://` URIs. The check is implemented as a textual `str.startswith` prefix match, so a URL such as `http://localhost:80@evil.example/cb` — whose actual host is `evil.example` and whose scheme…
items.summary: A prefix-matching vulnerability in Authlib's loopback transport check allows attackers to bypass secure transport constraints. Upgrade authlib to 1.8.0 or later.

items.title: dnspython dns.name.from_wire_parser() excessive CPU use
items.snippet: A maliciously crafted DNS message may cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression. There are no known workarounds. Evgenios Gkritsis, Department of Informatics, University of Piraeus & Athe…
items.summary: Malicious DNS wire-format messages can trigger excessive CPU usage during decompression in dnspython, causing a denial of service. Upgrade dnspython to 2.9.0 or later.

items.summary: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the MongoDB Python driver BSON decoder affects applications processing untrusted BSON data. Upgrade pymongo to 4.18.3 or later.

items.title: Strands Agents: Local Privilege Escalation via Symlink Attack in Default Session File Storage

items.summary: A symbolic link vulnerability in the default session file storage of Strands Agents allows local privilege escalation. Upgrade strands-agents to 1.48.0 or later.

items.title: Strands Agents: Default FileSessionManager storage is world-readable on shared systems
items.snippet: There is a local confidentiality issue in the default `FileSessionManager` storage behavior. By default it writes session data under `/tmp/strands/sessions` and relies on the process umask for directory and file permissions. On systems using the common `umask 022`, the session directories are `0755` and JSON files are `0644`, so other local users can read persisted agent session data. This matter…
items.summary: Insecure default permissions on session storage directories in Strands Agents expose sensitive data to local users on shared systems. Upgrade strands-agents to 1.48.0 or later.

items.summary: The undici package is vulnerable to cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via cross-origin redirects when using shared caches. JavaScript and Node.js developers using undici are affected. Upgrade undici to 7.30.1, 8.12.2 or later.

items.summary: Unauthenticated MLflow tracking servers are vulnerable to arbitrary file read via prompt model version sources using local paths. Systems running unauthenticated MLflow servers are affected. Upgrade mlflow to 3.17.0 or later.

items.summary: The mlflow.crewai.autolog() function leaks CrewAI LLM provider API keys into MLflow trace telemetry. Developers using CrewAI with MLflow autologging are affected. Upgrade mlflow to 3.17.0 or later.

items.snippet: MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. items.summary: MLflow allows remote code execution on unauthenticated servers through third-party scorer deserialization. Systems running unauthenticated OSS MLflow are at risk. Upgrade mlflow to 3.17.0 or later.

Attacker-controlled baggage could cause unnecessary CPU work and short-lived heap allocations while processing more data than the propagator should accept. Services that enable the optional Jaeger propagator and accept untrusted inbound propagation headers…
items.summary: Unbounded memory allocation in Jaeger baggage propagation can lead to CPU work and heap allocations from attacker-controlled headers. Applications using OpenTelemetry Python Jaeger propagator are affected. Upgrade opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger to 1.45.0 or later.

items.summary: MCP Python SDK HTTP client transports follow cross-origin redirects while carrying custom headers and bodies. Applications using the MCP Python client are affected. Upgrade mcp to 2.2.0, 1.30.0 or later.

items.title: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: Client fetched server-chosen $ref URLs while validating tool results against output schemas
items.snippet: In affected versions, when a connected MCP server declared an `outputSchema` for a tool, the SDK's client validated each `call_tool` result with `jsonschema`'s default resolver, which fetches any `$ref` it cannot resolve locally by opening the URL. items.summary: The MCP Python SDK client fetches server-chosen $ref URLs while validating tool results against output schemas. Applications using the MCP Python client are affected. Upgrade mcp to 2.2.0, 1.30.0 or later.
